CAD drawings under floor plans, config backups from Oxidized, end-of-life data, a personal sidebar, SFTP backups, bulk editing on the routing and power lists, and every bug report filed since 0.17.2.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scripts: the sandbox default is now `auto`.** Where bubblewrap works (`install.sh` installs it, and the Docker image has it), sandboxed scripts run in their own namespaces and can reach **only the Danbyte API**, not devices or other hosts. A sandboxed script that talks to devices directly needs `DANBYTE_SCRIPT_SANDBOX=landlock`, which keeps the 0.17.2 behaviour. Trusted scripts are unchanged. The stock Docker stack falls back to Landlock, because Docker's default profiles block bubblewrap.

> [!NOTE]
> **Behaviour changes:**
> - **FHRP authentication keys** move into the secret store during the upgrade (the built-in encrypted local store when none is configured) and are shown only through an audited Reveal. Old change-log entries are masked.
> - **Spreadsheet import** saves through the same rules as the API: read-only columns are ignored, four types are export-only (ACME orders, certificate bindings, floor plan drawings, Redfish endpoints), and a dry run applies the same checks as the real import.
> - **Single deletes** of routing objects still in use are refused with the reason, like bulk delete.
> - **Deleting a port** also removes a cable left with no port on that end.
> - **A JSON body that isn't an object** gets one shared 400 shape (`non_field_errors`) on every endpoint.

### CAD drawings in floor plans

- **Upload a DXF, or a DWG,** as a floor plan's background. LibreDWG's `dwg2dxf` converts DWG; `DANBYTE_CAD_CONVERTER` can point at the ODA File Converter instead.
- **True scale:** the drawing's units line up with the grid's cell size; unitless files are calibrated with two clicks. **Fit grid to drawing** sizes the grid from it.
- **Wrong units in the file:** pick what the drawing is really drawn in (mm, cm, m, in, ft); a drawing implausibly small or large for a floor plan gets a warning with the unit that fixes it in one click.
- **Layers panel** with show and hide, an "Architecture only" preset and a text toggle. Default-colour lines follow the light or dark theme.
- **In every view:** the editor, the 3D room floor, PNG export and the new **vector PDF export** (A4/A3/Letter/Tabloid, scale bar, legend, title block).
- **Editor:** undo and redo (100 steps), multi-select with move, rotate and delete, and a better "Find on plan".

### Features

- #98 - **VMware Cloud Director sync, finished:** VM groups (vApps) get list and detail pages, filters and search; Proxmox pools and vCenter folders sync into the same groups; NICs are read once per vApp instead of once per VM, so large estates stay inside the sync timeout.
- #35 - **Device config backups from Oxidized:** current config, history and diffs on a device's Config tab. Reading configs needs the new `view_config` permission, which no built-in role includes.
- #384 - **Oxidized nodes can be linked to virtual machines,** so virtual routers and firewalls get config backups too. Reading a VM's config needs `view_config` on virtual machines.
- #385 - **Automatic Oxidized node sync** every 5 to 60 minutes per connection (new connections every 30; existing ones stay off until turned on).
- #421 - **Support & warranty coverage:** support contracts per manufacturer with the devices they cover (picked or matched by serial number), a warranty end date per device, and a Covered / Expiring / Expired / Not covered status on the device page, as a device list column and filter, in a dashboard widget, in notifications and the digest, and as a compliance check.
- #8 - **End-of-life data from endoflife.date,** off by default: map platforms to products, see status on platforms and as a device/VM column, and add an end-of-life compliance check. Airgapped installs can import the catalog from a file.
- #285 - **Personal sidebar:** hide and reorder sections and pages under Preferences, with a tenant default. Long list filters get a search box and can be hidden per list.
- #319 - **SFTP backup destination,** with host-key confirmation, schedules and retention. Passphrase-protected OpenSSH keys work.
- #313 - **Power panels and feeds:** multi-select, bulk edit and safe bulk delete. Power panels can have a location.
- #314 - **All 17 routing lists:** multi-select, bulk edit and safe bulk delete with a preview of what is kept.
- #344 - **MAC address list:** a Location column showing where each MAC was learned.
- #345 - **Device components:** Front ports and Rear ports get their own tabs, and every component table gets the column picker.
- #394 - **Move a rack to another site** with all its devices, after a preview that lists anything still tied to the old site.
- #396 - **Copy buttons** on site and contact addresses.
- #419 - **Bulk SNMP actions on the drift page:** Poll, Refresh MACs and Sync from SNMP for selected devices or all of them, run in the background with one progress toast. Hovering "N drifted" shows what differs.
- #276 - **Searchable pickers on every object field,** with colour badges kept.
- #432 - **Circuits can end on a VM interface,** for cloud routers such as a CHR, pfSense or VyOS: pick the VM and its interface on the termination. The VM's interfaces show the circuit, the site map names the VM at that end, and circuit SLAs measure its addresses.
- **Device-type bundles can carry their photos** (base64), so a library moves between installs with its pictures and calibration.
- **Scheduled SNMP polling from the core** (Off / 15 / 30 / 60 minutes), skipping devices bound to an Outpost.
- **Live traffic on the site map:** a Utilization colour mode, each line split by direction.
- **Per-tenant rack capacity levels** (replacing the fixed 80/95 %) and a **rack power budget**.
- **SLA:** incident causes, ticket links and dispute flags; scheduled weekly and monthly reports; agreement templates; CSV/JSON metrics export.
- **Tasks tab on object pages** lists the open tasks linked to the object. A linked task past its due time shows a warning to its assignees, which each can dismiss until the due date moves.
- **List filters stay in the address:** facets, the search box and the advanced filter survive reload and Back and travel in a link (`/devices?status=active&tag=core`). A tag chip in a list filters it by that tag, a tag on an object's page opens its list filtered by it, and a ticked tag links to everything carrying it.
- **Search boxes on long detail tables:** a rack's devices, a virtualization source's VMs, hosts and review, device interfaces, change logs and about 50 other tabs. The search matches what the table shows, including related names.
- **Pick several objects at once** with the checkbox picker when linking objects to a task, marking maintenance impact, adding SLA members, adding ARP sources and assigning IPs to a DNS name.
- **DWG drawings work on every install:** the converter ships in the release bundle (static LibreDWG `dwg2dxf`, with its licence and source), so fresh installs and bundle upgrades need no setup, airgapped ones included. Source checkouts build it with `make cad-tools`; a set `DANBYTE_CAD_CONVERTER` still wins.

### Security

- #413 - **A site-limited user no longer reads other sites' IP addresses:** an address belongs to its prefix's site when it has none of its own, and a visible address leaves out devices, interfaces, prefixes and VMs the user can't see, in the API, exports and search.
- #413 - **The change log and search no longer name related objects a user can't see:** history shows such a device, interface or prefix as "hidden" (no name, no id), and search doesn't find a visible address by a hidden device's name.
- #414 - **Site limits cover every site-bound type:** services, NAT rules, VLAN groups, IP ranges, virtual chassis, config snapshots and about twenty more. A test fails if a new type is left out.
- #426 - **Site limits and row constraints apply to circuit, tunnel and L2VPN terminations, BGP address families, redistributions, IGP interfaces and VTEP memberships:** a user limited to one site could list, read and delete other sites' rows. A circuit, tunnel or L2VPN lists only the ends the user can see, and a test fails if a site-bound list skips the check.
- #415 - **Site viewers and "own sites only" editors can open, list and pick their own sites,** imports included. Existing site roles get it on upgrade.
- **A sandboxed script can no longer read the server's files through a link in its outputs:** the worker collected outputs by following links, so a script could copy `.env` or the worker's environment into a download.
- **The DWG converter's result is copied without following a link,** so a converter taken over by a crafted file can't have the worker read another file.
- **The change log leaves SLA service credits and fees out** for users without `view_credits`, as the agreement itself does.
- #424 - **The DWG converter runs in a bubblewrap sandbox:** no network, no access to the app directory, `.env` or media. Without a working bubblewrap, DWG is refused unless `DANBYTE_CAD_SANDBOX=off`; in Docker that means the `workers` profile change the script sandbox uses.
- #421 - **A support contract's cost needs the new *view cost* permission** to see or change it, in the API, exports, list columns and the change log. Superusers and the built-in Administrator group see it; Operator, Read-only and the site roles don't.
- **Export and label templates no longer print what the API hides from the person running them:** contract cost without *view cost*, SLA credits without *view credits*, and devices, contracts or prefixes the user can't see. Coverage rows no longer name a contract the user can't see, and contract device counts and the `?device=` / `?site=` filters count only visible devices.
- #425 - **Site viewers and "own sites only" editors read the catalogs their objects use** (device types, roles, platforms, statuses, tags, custom fields and the like), so Add device and an import by name work. View only; with enhanced site separation on, only global entries and their own sites' local ones. Existing site roles get it on upgrade.
- #316 - **Sandboxed scripts run in bubblewrap** (namespaces, no network but the API) on top of 0.17.2's Landlock confinement. See the note at the top.
- #364 - **Spreadsheet import can no longer mark a script trusted.**
- #365 - **Spreadsheet import can no longer point a credential at another Vault path.**
- #383 - **FHRP authentication keys are stored in the secret store** and revealed only with the reveal permission.
- **WinRM and vSphere connections are pinned to the checked address**; SSO and SAML addresses that resolve to a private network log a warning.
- **Container images publish only after the test suite passes** for that tag.
- **Smaller permission fixes:** bulk-cloning interfaces needs *add*; bulk-deleting watched endpoints needs *delete*, with a change-log entry per endpoint; the compliance violation list and Oxidized's unmatched-node reasons name only devices and VMs you can view; reprocessing a CAD drawing already queued queues nothing more, and a drawing's server renders queue at most three at once.

### Fixed

- #366 - **Moving a module to another bay, or changing its type, keeps its interfaces** with their cables, IPs and links. Removing ports that carry a cable or IP needs confirmation.
- #367 - **Bulk-cloned interfaces no longer belong to the module** of the interface they were cloned from.
- #368 - **Grouped topology no longer fails** for a user whose permission has an empty list constraint.
- #369 - **One refused PagerDuty event no longer drops the rest of a grouped alert burst;** refused events are retried.
- #370 - **An import file without a key column updates existing rows again.**
- #371 - **Objects named "Global", "None" or "-" survive an unchanged re-import.**
- #372 - **Deep IP list pages are as fast as the first.**
- #373 - **Malformed request bodies and parameters get a 400, not a 500,** on every endpoint.
- #374 - **Workbooks that unpack too large are refused** before they are read.
- #375 - **A full-depth device blocks the opposite face** of its units.
- #376 - **A rack can't be made shorter than its installed devices.**
- #377 - **A device can't be put in a rack at another site.**
- #378 - **Cables can't lose an end or connect incompatible ports.** `manage.py check_dcim_integrity` lists existing problems.
- #379 - **IP ranges can't overlap or sit outside their prefix.**
- #380 - **Shrinking a prefix or VLAN group is refused while something would be left outside;** VLANs already stranded can be edited again.
- #381 - **Aggregates are stored in canonical form and their utilisation counts each network once.** `manage.py check_aggregates` lists stored duplicates the upgrade couldn't merge.
- #382 - **IPv6 utilisation, next available and search agree.**
- #386 - **Pinning an Oxidized node can no longer reveal another object's config;** pinning needs connection rights and links follow site scope.
- #387 - **Spreadsheet export leaves out the columns the API hides from you,** such as SLA service credits.
- #388 - **Import and export are refused for an integration that is switched off.**
- #389 - **Records created before 0.18 can be saved from their edit forms;** the 0.18 rules run only when a field they depend on changes.
- #390 - **Changing a device type is refused when its racked devices would no longer fit.**
- #391 - **The bulk-delete preview counts the cables a delete removes.**
- #392 - **Swapping a cable's two ends in one edit works.**
- #393 - **The MAC address list is several times faster** on large tenants.
- #325 - **Virtual machines poll SNMP through their site's Outpost,** on the same engine as devices, and their SNMP page says where they poll from.
- #398, #399, #400 - **Oxidized links stay matched when a namesake appears, re-pinning after an unlink gets the same check as a move, and a new match for a node Oxidized already knew is proposed until someone confirms it.**
- #401 - **The email template preview shows behind nginx and other reverse proxies.**
- #402 - **MAC tables are read on Cisco switches with no IP in VLAN 1:** the switch's own VLANs are read first, and VLANs a VTP domain lists but the switch has no port in are skipped instead of ending the read.
- #403, #404, #407 - **Moving a rack checks cabinet-mounted bay children, split stacks and site-local tags, VRFs and roles on components, and names only objects you may see.**
- **The label template form no longer crashes when you add a device type,** and role pickers show each role's colour.
- #418 - **The sidebar lights one entry at a time:** Calendar no longer lights Planning as well.
- #420 - **OpenStreetMap address and boundary searches answer in your browser's language,** or English, instead of each place's local language. Thanks @deku-m for the fix.
- #408 - **A VLAN the switch is known to carry is retried when its MAC table doesn't answer,** and fails the read if it stays silent.
- #409 - **Moving a rack checks every site-local catalog** its rows point at, manufacturers on inventory items included, and the routing rows that move with the devices.
- #410 - **A stale check goes down again when staleness is turned off.**
- #411 - **A connection that synced on an 0.18 pre-release keeps proposing new Oxidized matches,** so a node missing from one sync can't be linked unchecked later.
- #412 - **Lists cut off at their load limit say so:** "1,000 of 40,960", a notice to search, and facet counts and downloads marked partial.
- #416 - **The device and VM list's monitoring column runs one query** instead of one per row.
- #417 - **The device page and the site map load only the cables they draw.**
- #427 - **The virtual machine list no longer runs a query per VM** for its cluster's status.
- #430 - **The prefix list's Monitoring and SLA columns fill on tenants with thousands of prefixes,** and the monitoring roll-up no longer reads every address of the tenant once per prefix. The column's address count now counts only addresses with a check, as its hover says.
- #431 - **Rack elevations load every rack's devices in one request** instead of one per rack.
- #428 - **Form labels name their fields:** clicking a label focuses its field, screen readers announce pickers by their label, and hints and errors are read with the field.
- #429 - **An integration's pages say it is off** instead of showing the API's 404 and an Add button, with a link to Settings → Integrations for admins.
- #405, #406 - **A proposed Oxidized link no longer keeps a node from its confirmed device,** and after the upgrade nodes Danbyte hasn't seen yet are proposed rather than linked. A connection's first sync after the upgrade may propose nodes that appeared since its last sync.
- **Status changes made by bulk edit show by name in the change log,** like a single edit, including entries already logged.
- **IP status pickers list only statuses offered to IP addresses,** as every other status picker does.
- **A stale check stays stale until the address comes back up,** instead of dropping back to down after a single answer or a fast-probe pass.
- **Docker:** sandboxed scripts reach the API through the backend service.
- **vCenter platforms use VMware Tools' OS name** (for example "Microsoft Windows Server 2022 (64-bit)") instead of vCenter's internal code, which labels Server 2022 as `WINDOWS_SERVER_2021_64`. Platforms an earlier sync named after that code move to the real name on the next sync; platforms you picked are kept.
- **Existing Proxmox and vCenter sources start syncing VM groups** (pools and folders) on their next sync; turn off "Sync pools/folders/vApps as VM groups" on a source to keep them ungrouped.

### Upgrades

- **The built-in Administrator group sees SLA service credits and support-contract costs:** its grant gains *view credits* and *view cost*. Operator and Read-only stay without them; a copy of the Administrator grant, or one shared with another group, is left as it is.

- **Existing site roles gain view on their sites and the newly site-scoped types** (services, NAT rules and others), unless an admin removed a type from the role. Change-log entries of those types and of IP addresses get their object's site, so site-limited users see only their own sites' history.
- **Base images come from ECR Public,** not Docker Hub; `BASE_IMAGE_REGISTRY` points the build at another mirror.
- **`install.sh` installs bubblewrap** unless given `--without-bubblewrap`: DWG drawings convert only inside it. An existing install it is added to keeps its scripts on Landlock (`DANBYTE_SCRIPT_SANDBOX=landlock` goes into `.env`) unless `.env` already sets one. An in-app upgrade installs no packages: there, `sudo apt install bubblewrap` and restart to take DWG.
- **An empty `DANBYTE_CAD_CONVERTER` now means the bundled DWG converter;** set it to `off` to keep refusing DWG uploads.
- **Every NOT NULL column added since the previous release must have a database default,** so processes still running the old code keep working right after the migrations (checked by a test against the last release).

Thank you @deku-m, @jorge-madrigal, @SerhiiZahuba and @PVM-NL for the reports and requests.
